summary: Virginia is one of the clearest 'yes' states for the roof rat. Its wildlife code (4VAC15-20-50) literally names 'Domesticated races of rats (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus rattus)' as DOMESTIC animals, which removes captive-bred pet roof rats from the 'wild animal' and 'nonnative (exotic)' categories and from the Department of Wildlife Resources' permitting. The genus does not appear on the predatory/undesirable nonnative list. So keeping, breeding, and selling/giving a pet roof rat is legal with no wildlife permit. The only conditional requirement is a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection when importing one from out of state for sale, adoption, or breeding (a personal move-in is exempt). Never release one, wild R. rattus is a designated nuisance.

keep.why: Domesticated Rattus rattus is expressly defined as a 'domestic animal' in 4VAC15-20-50 (which lists 'Domesticated races of rats (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus rattus)'), removing it from the 'wild animal' and 'nonnative (exotic) animal' definitions and thus from DWR possession-permit requirements. The genus does not appear on the predatory/undesirable nonnative list (4VAC15-30-40). No permit is required to keep one. Gemini DR-verified: 4VAC15-20-50 explicitly lists 'Domesticated races of rats (R. norvegicus and R. rattus)' as domestic animals (protection applies to captive-bred lineage).
keep.governing_law: 4VAC15-20-50 (domestic-animal list incl. R. rattus; definitions); 4VAC15-30-40 (permit list, Rattus absent).

breed.why: Because the species is a domestic animal outside DWR jurisdiction, breeding needs no DWR wildlife/propagation permit (the breeding restriction in 4VAC15-20-50(B) names only foxes and rabbits, not rats). No species-specific Virginia breeding ban exists. Large-scale commercial breeding could implicate general VDACS animal-dealer/pet-shop provisions and local zoning, activity-scale rules, not species rules. Gemini DR-verified: no state breeder license for companion rodents; only general welfare standards apply.
breed.governing_law: 4VAC15-20-50 (domestic-animal status); general commercial-animal provisions, Code of Va. Title 3.2 Subtitle V.

sell_give.why: DWR sale/possession permits (4VAC15-30-40) apply only to listed predatory/undesirable nonnative exotics; R. rattus is a domestic animal and not on that list, so no DWR sale permit applies. There is no Virginia prohibition on selling or giving away domestic pet rodents. Standard pet-dealer/consumer rules and the import-CVI-for-sale rule (below) apply to the transaction, not the species. Gemini DR-verified: legal; commercial sellers ('dealers') may need a LOCAL pet-shop/dealer permit (fee capped at $50).
sell_give.governing_law: 4VAC15-30-40(C) (non-listed nonnative animals may be possessed/purchased/sold); 4VAC15-20-50; Code of Va. §3.2-5902.

transport.why: Intrastate transport of a domestic pet rat is unregulated by DWR. For IMPORT from another state, Code of Va. §3.2-5902 requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (dated within 10 days) for a pet animal, but it EXEMPTS animals merely passing through and animals brought in by a resident or someone moving to Virginia, EXCEPT when brought in to offer for public sale, trade, or promotion. So: personal move-in = no CVI; import to sell/adopt-out/breed-for-sale = CVI required. Gemini DR-verified: commercial import needs a CVI issued within 10 days; a resident relocating with a personal pet rat is exempt. Intrastate legal.
transport.governing_law: Code of Va. §3.2-5902 (CVI for imported pet animals; resident/transit exemptions).

restrictions.summary: A Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (within 10 days) is required to import a pet roof rat into Virginia FOR SALE, adoption, breeding, or promotion. Bringing your own pet in when you move (personal ownership) is exempt, as is merely passing through.
steps: For a personal move-in: no CVI needed
To import for sale/adoption/breeding: get a CVI within 10 days

restrictions.summary: Although domestic in status, releasing any roof rat into the wild is prohibited (4VAC15-30-40(C) no-liberation rule), and wild R. rattus is a designated nuisance species (4VAC15-20-160). Never release; rehome responsibly.
